title: Represent recoverable failure explicitly

triggers: fallible operations, untrusted input, external boundaries, unwrap, expect, panic, indexing

requirement: Recoverable failures must be represented with Result, Option, or a repository-defined equivalent. Panics and panic-capable convenience operations are reserved for proven programming errors or explicit termination policy, with the invariant made visible.

mechanical_enforcement.check: selective clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, and clippy::indexing_slicing
mechanical_enforcement.caveat: Tests, const contexts, poisoned locks, and proven invariants require repository-specific policy; do not enable the restriction group wholesale.
These diagnose absent sections, not complete or correct failure contracts, and grant no repair authority.

completion_evidence: panic-capable site review for changed scope

action_overrides.reason: Defining or changing foreign error signaling, sentinel values, out-parameters, callbacks, or ABI status semantics changes the caller contract.

remediation.guidance: Propagate or translate recoverable errors with context. Retain a panic only when the violated programming invariant and termination intent are explicit.

authoring_projection: Classify each new failure as recoverable, programmer error, or process-fatal policy before choosing Result, Option, assertion, or panic.
At external and untrusted-input boundaries, propagate contextual errors instead of unwrap or expect.
